title: Introduce request-windowing and layered prefix cache slimming to reduce console aggregation fanout
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: The console API aggregation path is experiencing high fanout for short-lived bursts (spikes from UI autos-refresh and polling routes). This leads to excessive downstream GraphQL resolver invocations and repeated cold reads from the prefix/KV cache layer, manifesting as elevated p95 latency and occasional OOMs in the aggregation worker.

Goal: Implement a thin, backwards-compatible request-windowing layer to coalesce near-simultaneous requests for the same entity keys, plus a layered prefix cache slimming strategy: (1) introduce a fast in-memory L1 with stricter TTLs for hot short-lived reads, (2) retain the existing L2 persistent cache for larger/heavier entries, and (3) add an adaptive sampling pass to prune oversized prefix entries. Together these should reduce redundant resolver work and memory churn without changing GraphQL schema or caller semantics.

Scope: backend-only changes affecting console aggregation service and the GraphQL resolver hydration pipeline. No client changes. Includes small dependency bump (graphql-js 16.x -> 17.x) to address a memory leak in resolver instrumentation and Node 18 -> 20 runtime support for worker threads.

Non-goals: full aggregator rewrite, changes to UI polling frequency, or altering public API payload shapes.
acceptance_criteria: p95 end-to-end console API latency for aggregation endpoints reduced by >=20% under synthetic burst tests
aggregation worker memory usage reduced by >=25% during 30s spike replay
no API contract changes (GraphQL schema identical), all existing e2e tests pass
new L1/L2 cache toggleable via feature flag and rolloutable per-cluster
benchmark doc with before/after traces and cost estimate added to Confluence
comments: 2026-02-26 - Asha: Spike completed. Request-windowing approach using 50ms coalescing showed 28% fewer resolver executions in local replay. Observed occasional added scheduling latency (~3ms) which is acceptable. Added notes in design doc.

2026-03-01 - Devs: Started implementation of L1 (bounded LRU) and adapter to L2 persistent prefix cache. L1 implemented as actor-local fast map with async fallback. Working on graceful eviction hooks for large prefix entries.

2026-03-04 - QA: End-to-end synthetic burst harness (k6) results: p95 reduced ~22% on dev cluster for dashboard-aggregation route; however tail CPU spikes observed in aggregator pod during L2 misses. Investigating whether we need backpressure on deserialization path.
2026-03-07 - Security: Verified no new network endpoints. Dependency bump to graphql-js@17 flagged for regen of lockfile and Audit-Note added (GH-PR-42).

2026-03-10 - PR: Opened PR #5123 with implementation and feature flag. Requesting code review from @maria and @jordan. Added integration test that replays historical incident trace (inc-2025-11-03) to validate memory profile.

2026-03-12 - PM (Renee): Approved tradeoffs for default rollout to internal-only clusters first. Plan for gradual rollout to prod if metrics meet thresholds during 72h canary. Added to release notes draft.
